Definition: of Hebrew origin (H7018); Cainan (i.e. Kenan), the name of two patriarchs:--Cainan.
BiblicalUsage: Cainan is the name of two men in the genealogy of Jesus, one the son of Arphaxad and the other the son of Enos. Luke names them both as he traces the line back from Jesus through the patriarchs to Adam.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the two Cainans show how carefully Luke traced the line of the Saviour: no generation is skipped, and every name in the chain matters because the promise ran through every one of them.
